import sqlite3
import uuid
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Header, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import List, Optional
import uvicorn

DATABASE = "db.sqlite3"

def get_db():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DATABASE)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    return conn

def init_db():
    conn = get_db()
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    cursor.execute("""
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS listings (
            listing_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            description TEXT NOT NULL,
            address TEXT NOT NULL,
            city TEXT NOT NULL,
            creator_id TEXT NOT NULL
        )
    """)
    cursor.execute("""
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS invited_helpers (
            listing_id TEXT NOT NULL,
            helper_id TEXT NOT NULL,
            PRIMARY KEY (listing_id, helper_id),
            FOREIGN KEY (listing_id) REFERENCES listings(listing_id)
        )
    """)
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    init_db()
    yield

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

class CreateListingRequest(BaseModel):
    description: str
    address: str
    invited_helper_ids: List[str]   # now required

class ListingResponse(BaseModel):
    description: str
    city: str
    creator_id: str

def extract_city(address: str) -> str:
    # Simple city extraction: take the part after the last comma, or the whole address
    parts = [p.strip() for p in address.split(",")]
    if len(parts) >= 2:
        return parts[-1]  # City is the last segment
    return address

@app.post("/listings", status_code=201)
async def create_listing(
    body: CreateListingRequest,
    x_user_id: str = Header(..., alias="X-User-ID")
):
    if not body.description or not body.address:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Description and address are required")
    
    listing_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    city = extract_city(body.address)
    
    conn = get_db()
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    try:
        cursor.execute(
            "INSERT INTO listings (listing_id, description, address, city, creator_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (listing_id, body.description, body.address, city, x_user_id)
        )
        for helper_id in body.invited_helper_ids:
            cursor.execute(
                "INSERT INTO invited_helpers (listing_id, helper_id) VALUES (?, ?)",
                (listing_id, helper_id)
            )
        conn.commit()
    except Exception as e:
        conn.rollback()
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e))
    finally:
        conn.close()
    
    return {"listing_id": listing_id}

@app.get("/listings/{listing_id}", response_model=ListingResponse)
async def get_listing(
    listing_id: str,
    x_user_id: str = Header(..., alias="X-User-ID")
):
    conn = get_db()
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    # Get listing
    cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM listings WHERE listing_id = ?", (listing_id,))
    listing = cursor.fetchone()
    
    if not listing:
        conn.close()
        # Return 403 to avoid leaking existence, as per spec "Otherwise returns 403"
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="User is not authorized to view this listing")
    
    # Check if user is creator
    if listing["creator_id"] == x_user_id:
        conn.close()
        return ListingResponse(
            description=listing["description"],
            city=listing["city"],
            creator_id=listing["creator_id"]
        )
    
    # Check if user is invited helper
    cursor.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM invited_helpers WHERE listing_id = ? AND helper_id = ?",
        (listing_id, x_user_id)
    )
    helper = cursor.fetchone()
    conn.close()
    
    if helper:
        return ListingResponse(
            description=listing["description"],
            city=listing["city"],
            creator_id=listing["creator_id"]
        )
    
    raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="User is not authorized to view this listing")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=5000)
